items.title: Android Stress Detection
items.subtitle: Wearable PPG Signal Processing, On-Device ONNX Inference & Decision Support
items.summary: Wearable PPG signal processing and on-device ONNX stress detection across Android and Galaxy Watch, paired with local AI counseling and signal quality gating.
items.description: Dual-module Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, and Wear OS research prototype recording multi-channel PPG from Samsung Galaxy Watch and running channel-independent ONNX Runtime inference locally on Android, with explicit abstain logic when signal quality is insufficient.
items.personalContribution: Built the multi-module Phone and Wear OS Kotlin apps, on-device signal gating and ONNX Runtime wrappers, local RAG AI+ counselor, Verbatim+ audio features, R8 hardening, and CI publication-safety scans.
items.problemStatement: Wearable PPG recordings suffer from motion artifacts, cadence jitter, and transport gaps, while streaming physiological signals to cloud backends introduces acute privacy risks.
items.proposedSolution: Split raw Galaxy Watch PPG acquisition from Android-side validation, SQA/MADC gating, and channel-independent Green/IR ONNX Runtime inference so the app abstains with INSUFFICIENT_SIGNAL rather than fabricating predictions.
items.architectureSummary: Four-module Gradle architecture (app, wear, shared, inference) using MVVM + unidirectional Flow, Google Play Services Wear Data Layer, Room persistence, local Gemma/LiteRT-LM counseling, and Sherpa-ONNX speech components.
implementedFeatures: Samsung Galaxy Watch PPG recording over Wear Data Layer with independent Green and IR channel evaluation
On-device signal quality assessment (SQA/MADC), 240s anchor core windowing, and strict abstain handling on insufficient signal
Local ONNX Runtime inference locked to validated biosignal pipeline contracts (ECG used only as offline research validation reference)
Five-tab Jetpack Compose interface (Home, History, Verbatim+, AI+ local RAG counselor, Profile) with R8 release hardening and SHA-256 asset verification
items.testingStrategy: 868 JVM unit tests passing across app (796), inference (34), and shared (38) modules on v0.1.5, alongside ktlint, detekt, production lint, Gitleaks full-history scan, and physical Xiaomi device UI smoke verification.
items.resultsAndLimitations: This project is an experimental research prototype for stress monitoring and decision support, not a medical diagnostic tool. Phone v0.1.5 and Watch v0.1.1 are internal debug previews; full-channel Watch acceptance remains partial due to diagnostic Red timestamp conflicts, and AI+ local corpus/web citations are not clinically validated.

personalProjects.title: Android Stress Detection
personalProjects.subtitle: Wearable PPG Signal Processing, On-Device ONNX Inference & Decision Support
personalProjects.summary: Wearable PPG signal processing and on-device ONNX stress detection across Android and Galaxy Watch, paired with local AI counseling and signal quality gating.
personalProjects.description: Dual-module Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, and Wear OS research prototype recording multi-channel PPG from Samsung Galaxy Watch and running channel-independent ONNX Runtime inference locally on Android, with explicit abstain logic when signal quality is insufficient.
personalProjects.personalContribution: Built the multi-module Phone and Wear OS Kotlin apps, on-device signal gating and ONNX Runtime wrappers, local RAG AI+ counselor, Verbatim+ audio features, R8 hardening, and CI publication-safety scans.
personalProjects.problemStatement: Wearable PPG recordings suffer from motion artifacts, cadence jitter, and transport gaps, while streaming physiological signals to cloud backends introduces acute privacy risks.
personalProjects.proposedSolution: Split raw Galaxy Watch PPG acquisition from Android-side validation, SQA/MADC gating, and channel-independent Green/IR ONNX Runtime inference so the app abstains with INSUFFICIENT_SIGNAL rather than fabricating predictions.
personalProjects.architectureSummary: Four-module Gradle architecture (app, wear, shared, inference) using MVVM + unidirectional Flow, Google Play Services Wear Data Layer, Room persistence, local Gemma/LiteRT-LM counseling, and Sherpa-ONNX speech components.
implementedFeatures: Samsung Galaxy Watch PPG recording over Wear Data Layer with independent Green and IR channel evaluation
On-device signal quality assessment (SQA/MADC), 240s anchor core windowing, and strict abstain handling on insufficient signal
Local ONNX Runtime inference locked to validated biosignal pipeline contracts (ECG used only as offline research validation reference)
Five-tab Jetpack Compose interface (Home, History, Verbatim+, AI+ local RAG counselor, Profile) with R8 release hardening and SHA-256 asset verification
personalProjects.testingStrategy: 868 JVM unit tests passing across app (796), inference (34), and shared (38) modules on v0.1.5, alongside ktlint, detekt, production lint, Gitleaks full-history scan, and physical Xiaomi device UI smoke verification.
personalProjects.resultsAndLimitations: This project is an experimental research prototype for stress monitoring and decision support, not a medical diagnostic tool. Phone v0.1.5 and Watch v0.1.1 are internal debug previews; full-channel Watch acceptance remains partial due to diagnostic Red timestamp conflicts, and AI+ local corpus/web citations are not clinically validated.

resources.title: Coffee Brew Ratio, Extraction Yield & Recipe Scaler
resources.summary: Brew ratio equals water mass divided by dry dose (1:W/D), while cup-only Extraction Yield (EY%) equals (Measured Beverage Mass x Measured TDS%) / Dry Dose. For multi-pour V60 recipes, Hamilton-Hare largest-remainder rounding keeps scaled pour steps equal to the exact target water mass.

resources.title: Perfume Concentration & Dilution Batch Calculator
resources.summary: Fragrance concentration equals (Non-Solvent Fragrance Oil Mass / Total Formula Weight) x 100%. Standard classification brackets treat >=20% as Parfum Extrait, 15%–20% as Eau de Parfum (EDP), 8%–15% as Eau de Toilette (EDT), 4%–8% as Eau de Cologne (EDC), and <4% as Eau Fraiche.

resources.title: AutomatePlus vs Selenium IDE vs Katalon Studio

resources.title: Playwright vs Cypress in CI/CD & Cross-Origin E2E
resources.summary: Choose Playwright for free cross-machine parallel sharding, WebKit coverage, multi-tab or multi-origin workflows, and multi-language teams (JS/TS, Python, Java, .NET). Choose Cypress when tight in-browser time-travel component debugging inside a single JS/TS frontend repository outweighs multi-tab or paid cloud parallelization limits.
